title: Non-activating panel + paste into the target app
setup: Turn on clipboard history: press Win+V, then 'Turn on' (needed to check the item never shows up in history).
Open a normal (non-admin) Notepad and a Windows Terminal / PowerShell window.
Have Chrome, Word and Paint available. Optional: Excel, KeePass, Remote Desktop.

tests.title: Panel opens without stealing focus
tests.do: Click this terminal window, then click an EMPTY area of the Snipdeck panel (not an item yet: this terminal is the paste target, so clicking an item would type into the wizard). The panel footer should read 'Pastes into WindowsTerminal.exe'.
tests.expect: The panel appears WITHOUT taking focus from the terminal. No 'entry point not found' error. No taskbar button (note any brief flash at start-up). Not listed in Alt+Tab. Stays above other windows. Clicking the panel leaves the terminal's title bar active.

tests.title: Notepad: click an item to paste
tests.do: Copy the word BEFORE to the clipboard. In Notepad type abc. Click 'Hello from Snipdeck' in the panel. Then press Ctrl+V in Notepad. Open Win+V history.
tests.expect: Footer before click: 'Pastes into Notepad.exe ...' with NO '(no caret seen)'. Text inserted at the caret, Notepad stays active with the caret blinking, status shows 'Pasted into ...'. Ctrl+V then pastes BEFORE (restore worked). Win+V history does NOT contain the item.

tests.title: Unicode and multi-line items
tests.do: Click the 'unicode' item (with the check mark, Japanese and emoji) and the two-line item.
tests.expect: Exact text, with line breaks intact.

tests.title: Shift+click copies only
tests.do: Hold Shift and click an item. Then press Ctrl+V in Notepad.
tests.expect: Nothing inserted on the click. Status says 'Copied (Shift+click)'. Ctrl+V then pastes the item.

tests.title: Alt and Win held while clicking
tests.do: Hold Alt and click an item. Then hold the Windows key and click an item. Release, then type normally.
tests.expect: Both paste. Notepad's menu bar is NOT activated (no underlined access keys) and the Start menu does NOT open. No stuck modifier keys afterwards.

tests.title: Ctrl held while clicking
tests.do: Hold Ctrl and click an item.
tests.expect: Pasted once. Ctrl is not stuck afterwards.

tests.title: Clipboard restore of images and files
tests.do: Copy an image in Paint, paste an item into Notepad, then Ctrl+V in Paint. Repeat with a file copied in Explorer, pasting back into a folder.
tests.expect: The image / file is back on the clipboard and pastes correctly.

tests.title: Dragging the panel (informational)
tests.do: Drag the panel by its title bar while Notepad is active.
tests.expect: Just record whether Notepad loses activation (the real product will be frameless).

tests.title: Word: paste and formatted restore
tests.do: Click into a Word document and repeat tests 2 to 2b. Then copy formatted text (bold plus a picture) in Word, paste an item into Notepad, and Ctrl+V back in Word.
tests.expect: Footer reports a caret and paste works. Formatting comes back after the restore. Record whether the picture is missing (EMF is not preserved). Optional: same with an Excel cell range.

tests.title: Chrome text field
tests.do: In Chrome click into a textarea (for example a GitHub comment box), then click an item. Repeat in the address bar.
tests.expect: Record the footer (caret seen, or '(no caret seen)'). The item is pasted at the caret.

tests.title: Typing in the panel's search box, then Enter
tests.do: Put the caret in the MIDDLE of the Chrome textarea text. Click the panel's Search field, type kind, press Enter. Repeat starting from the address bar.
tests.expect: Typing goes to the panel (Chrome's title bar is inactive while typing). The list filters to 'Kind regards'. Enter re-activates Chrome and inserts the text AT the old caret position without replacing the text. Record any select-all. Record whether the address bar contents get replaced.

tests.title: Search then Esc / click item / click Notepad
tests.do: Search, then press Esc. Search, then click an item. Search, then click into Notepad.
tests.expect: Esc: Chrome returns to the front with the caret where it was. Item click: pasted into Chrome. Notepad: Notepad stays in front (no bounce back to Chrome).

tests.title: Elevated Notepad (admin) falls back to copy
tests.do: Start Notepad with 'Run as administrator', click into it, then click an item. Press Ctrl+V manually.
tests.expect: Footer: 'Copies to clipboard (Notepad.exe runs as admin; Snipdeck does not)'. Status 'Copied: ...'. Nothing injected. Ctrl+V pastes the item manually.

tests.title: Same, but Snipdeck itself runs as admin
tests.do: Snipdeck was relaunched as administrator (accept the UAC prompt). Click into the admin Notepad and click an item.
tests.expect: Footer becomes 'Pastes into ...' and pasting works.

tests.title: Password fields
tests.do: Use a password input on a web login page in Chrome, and (if available) a Win32 password box such as the KeePass master-password dialog. Click an item.
tests.expect: Paste works and shows as masked characters. The item is NOT in Win+V history. After about 0.5 s, Ctrl+V elsewhere gives the previous clipboard. Record the footer caret state.

tests.title: Fullscreen apps
tests.do: With the panel visible, open a fullscreen video (YouTube, press f), a PowerPoint slideshow, or a fullscreen game by Alt+Tab or click. Then Alt+Tab away.
tests.expect: The panel hides while the fullscreen app is in front and reappears afterwards WITHOUT taking focus. Known gap: F11 inside an already-focused window does not hide the panel until the next foreground change. Record it.

tests.title: No text target
tests.do: Click the desktop, then an item. Also try Calculator.
tests.expect: Record the footer and what happens. Ideally nothing bad happens.

tests.title: Terminals
tests.do: Windows Terminal (PowerShell), then vim inside it. Click an item each time.
tests.expect: Record whether the paste works. Vim is expected to treat Ctrl+V as visual-block, which confirms the need for per-app paste keys.

tests.title: Slow target: Remote Desktop
tests.do: Paste into a Remote Desktop session.
tests.expect: Record whether the remote side receives the item or the OLD clipboard (restore-timing risk).
